First public release of **Tsuzuri 綴**, offline voice dictation for macOS. Licensed under **MIT**. The KanaWorks_AI brand assets (name, logo, the Kana character, the app icon and the banners) are not covered by the MIT license; see `docs/brand`.

## Dictation

- Menu bar app for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 14 Sonoma or later), no Dock icon.
- Hold the trigger key to talk and let go to insert the text, or tap it to start and tap again to stop. Right ⌥ Option by default; right ⌘ Command or Fn can be chosen from the menu.
- Esc, or pressing another key while holding the trigger (for example ⌥ + a letter), cancels, so your normal shortcuts keep working. Recordings stop automatically after 3 minutes.
- A small overlay that never takes focus shows "Listening…" with a live level meter, then "Transcribing…", then the result.
- Text is pasted into the focused app through the clipboard, so it works the same in every app and with Chinese or Japanese input methods turned on. Your previous clipboard is restored afterwards (except password-manager items, which are never put back, and very large clipboards).
- Nothing you said gets lost: if nothing editable has focus, the text is only copied and the overlay tells you to press ⌘V; if Tsuzuri can't tell (some Electron apps), it pastes and also leaves the text on the clipboard. The menu keeps your last 10 results (in memory only) for copying again. Text dictated into password fields is not shown or kept.
- Switching or unplugging the microphone mid-recording keeps what was already captured; Macs without a microphone show "No microphone found" instead of failing.

## Recognition

- Qwen3-ASR running locally through MLX Swift. No cloud, no account; audio is never written to disk or sent anywhere.
- 30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects, detected automatically for every dictation, tuned and tested for English, Japanese and Chinese, including mixing them in one sentence.
- Spoken Language menu: Auto, or pin one of the 30 languages (English, Japanese and Chinese first) when a short phrase comes out in the wrong language.
- Models: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (4-bit, default, more accurate) and 0.6B (8-bit, faster), plus 1.7B 8-bit and 0.6B 4-bit. Switch from the menu; the current model keeps working until the new one has loaded.
- Silero VAD trims silence before and after speech. Long dictations (up to the 3-minute limit) are recognized in pieces cut at your pauses, so they stay accurate.

Supported languages: Arabic, Cantonese, Chinese, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Filipino, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Macedonian, Malay, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese. Chinese dialects: Anhui, Dongbei, Fujian, Gansu, Guizhou, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Ningxia, Shandong, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Sichuan, Tianjin, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Cantonese (Hong Kong), Cantonese (Guangdong), Wu, Min Nan.

## Polish (optional, off by default)

- A second small local model, spokenly/cleanup-1 (converted to 4-bit MLX on your Mac), adds punctuation, removes filler words, keeps only the corrected version when you correct yourself, and writes numbers as digits. It never translates or answers.
- Only used for the languages the model was trained on: English, German, Spanish, French, Chinese, Russian and Japanese. Other languages are pasted exactly as recognized.
- Safety checks fall back to the raw transcript if the result is much longer, changes script, adds words or numbers you didn't say, or takes more than 1 second.
- Skipped in terminal apps (Terminal, iTerm2, Warp, Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm and others), where you usually dictate commands.

## Setup and privacy

- On first launch a "Set Up Tsuzuri" window walks you through the Microphone and Accessibility permissions and turns green when both are allowed. Until Accessibility is on (or if it is turned off later), the menu bar icon shows a warning badge and the first menu line opens the window; it can be reopened any time from Permissions….
- If a model is missing, the menu says so; a model downloaded later is picked up the next time you press the shortcut.
- `~/Library/Logs/Tsuzuri.log` records timings and errors, never what you said (unless you turn on `logText` for debugging). It is rotated at 5 MB (one old file is kept).
- Interface in 30 languages, following your macOS language: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Filipino, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Macedonian, Malay, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese.
- The app bundle includes the license and NOTICE texts of all bundled third-party code (`Contents/Resources/Licenses.txt`).

## Command line

- `tsuzuri-cli` transcribes audio files with the same engine: choose model and language, JSON Lines output with timings and memory use, optional Polish, or Polish on text only. Run `tsuzuri-cli --help`.

## Install

Download `Tsuzuri-1.0.0.dmg` below (signed and notarized by Apple) and drag Tsuzuri into Applications. Speech models are not bundled: download them as described in the [README](https://github.com/kanaworksai-hue/tsuzuri#-install) (about 1.6 GB for the default model).

**Known limits:** short Japanese phrases inside Chinese sentences are sometimes written in romaji or as Chinese sound-alikes; English loanwords in Japanese are often written in katakana; the paste shortcut assumes the QWERTY position of V.
